message.content:
Here’s a classic list of ingredients you’ll need to bake a rich, moist chocolate cake. Feel free to adjust quantities or add extras (like espresso powder or a splash of orange liqueur) to suit your taste. | Ingredient | Typical Amount (for a 9‑inch round cake, 2 layers) | Notes | |------------|----------------------------------------------|-------| | **All‑purpose flour** | 1 ¾ cups (220 g) | Sifted; keep it dry. | | **Cocoa powder** | ¾ cup (65 g) | Unsweetened, Dutch‑processed for a deeper flavor. | | **Granulated sugar** | 2 cups (400 g) | Gives sweetness and helps with browning. | | **Baking powder** | 1 ½ tsp | Leavening agent. | | **Baking soda** | 1 ½ tsp | Works with acidic cocoa. | | **Salt** | 1 tsp | Balances sweetness. | | **Eggs** | 2 large | Room temperature for better emulsion. | | **Whole milk** | 1 cup (240 ml) | Adds moisture; can substitute with buttermilk or a non‑dairy milk. | | **Vegetable oil** | ½ cup (120 ml) | Keeps cake tender; can use melted butter or coconut oil. | | **Vanilla extract** | 2 tsp | Enhances flavor. | | **Boiling water** | 1 cup (240 ml) | Activates cocoa, creates a lighter crumb. | | **Optional extras** | | • 1 tsp espresso powder (boosts chocolate flavor)
• ¼ cup chocolate chips or chopped nuts (for texture)
• 1 tbsp orange zest (adds brightness) | ### Quick Prep Tips 1. **Preheat** your oven to 350 °F (175 °C). 2. Grease and flour two 9‑inch round cake pans (or line with parchment). 3. Combine dry ingredients first, then wet ingredients separately. 4. Mix dry into wet until just combined; avoid over‑mixing. 5. Fold in boiling water last—this will make the batter thin but results in a moist cake. 6. Bake 25–30 min, or until a toothpick comes out clean. 7. Cool in pans 10 min, then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely before frosting. Enjoy your chocolate cake! If you’d like a specific frosting or glaze recipe, just let me know.
